#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to verify what is about to be committed.
# Called by "git commit" with no arguments.  The hook should
# exit with non-zero status after issuing an appropriate message if
# it wants to stop the commit.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "pre-commit".

if git rev-parse --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1
then
	against=HEAD
else
	# Initial commit: diff against an empty tree object
	against=$(git hash-object -t tree /dev/null)
fi

# If you want to allow non-ASCII filenames set this variable to true.
allownonascii=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allownonascii)

# Redirect output to stderr.
exec 1>&2

# Cross platform projects tend to avoid non-ASCII filenames; prevent
# them from being added to the repository. We exploit the fact that the
# printable range starts at the space character and ends with tilde.
if [ "$allownonascii" != "true" ] &&
	# Note that the use of brackets around a tr range is ok here, (it's
	# even required, for portability to Solaris 10's /usr/bin/tr), since
	# the square bracket bytes happen to fall in the designated range.
	test $(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=A -z $against |
	  LC_ALL=C tr -d '[ -~]\0' | wc -c) != 0
then
	cat <<\EOF
Error: Attempt to add a non-ASCII file name.

This can cause problems if you want to work with people on other platforms.

To be portable it is advisable to rename the file.

If you know what you are doing you can disable this check using:

  git config hooks.allownonascii true
EOF
	exit 1
fi

# If there are whitespace errors, print the offending file names and fail.
exec git diff-index --check --cached $against --

#!/bin/sh
#
# pre-commit hook: legacy validation and reporting logic.
# Called by "git commit" with no arguments.
# Exit with non-zero status to abort the commit.
#

LOGFILE="/tmp/pre-commit-report.log"
TIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
ERRORS=0

echo "========================================"  | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
echo "Pre-commit validation run: $TIMESTAMP"     | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
echo "========================================"  | tee -a "$LOGFILE"

# ── Resolve diff target ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if git rev-parse --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    against=HEAD
else
    # Initial commit: diff against an empty tree object
    against=$(git hash-object -t tree /dev/null)
fi

# Redirect output to stderr so it shows in the terminal during commit
exec 1>&2

# ── 1. Non-ASCII filename check ───────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "[CHECK] Non-ASCII filenames..." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
allownonascii=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allownonascii)

if [ "$allownonascii" != "true" ] &&
    test "$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=A -z "$against" |
      LC_ALL=C tr -d '[ -~]\0' | wc -c)" != 0
then
    echo "[FAIL]  Non-ASCII filename detected." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
    cat <<\EOF
Error: Attempt to add a non-ASCII file name.

This can cause problems if you want to work with people on other platforms.
To be portable it is advisable to rename the file.

If you know what you are doing you can disable this check using:
  git config hooks.allownonascii true
EOF
    ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
fi

# ── 2. Whitespace check ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "[CHECK] Whitespace errors..." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
if ! git diff-index --check --cached "$against" -- >> "$LOGFILE" 2>&1; then
    echo "[FAIL]  Whitespace errors found. See $LOGFILE for details." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
    git diff-index --check --cached "$against" --
    ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
fi

# ── 3. Syntax check: shell scripts ───────────────────────────────────────────
echo "[CHECK] Shell script syntax..." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM "$against" | grep -E '\.(sh|bash)$' | while read -r file; do
    if ! sh -n "$file" 2>>"$LOGFILE"; then
        echo "[FAIL]  Syntax error in shell script: $file" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
        ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
    else
        echo "[OK]    $file" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
    fi
done

# ── 4. Syntax check: Python scripts ──────────────────────────────────────────
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[CHECK] Python script syntax..." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
    git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM "$against" | grep -E '\.py$' | while read -r file; do
        if ! python3 -m py_compile "$file" 2>>"$LOGFILE"; then
            echo "[FAIL]  Syntax error in Python script: $file" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
            ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
        else
            echo "[OK]    $file" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
        fi
    done
fi

# ── 5. Detect debug / leftover markers ───────────────────────────────────────
echo "[CHECK] Debug markers (TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX/debugger/console.log)..." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
MARKERS=$(git diff --cached --unified=0 "$against" | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++' \
    | grep -iE '(TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX|debugger|console\.log)')
if [ -n "$MARKERS" ]; then
    echo "[WARN]  Debug/leftover markers found:" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
    echo "$MARKERS" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
    # Warning only — does not block commit
fi

# ── 6. File size guard (warn if any staged file > 5 MB) ──────────────────────
echo "[CHECK] Large file sizes (> 5 MB)..." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM "$against" | while read -r file; do
    if [ -f "$file" ]; then
        SIZE=$(wc -c < "$file")
        if [ "$SIZE" -gt 5242880 ]; then
            echo "[FAIL]  Large file staged: $file ($SIZE bytes)" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
            ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
        fi
    fi
done

# ── 7. Staged file report ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
echo "[REPORT] Staged files:" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
git diff --cached --name-status "$against" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"

# ── Summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
echo "----------------------------------------" | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
if [ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "[RESULT] $ERRORS error(s) found. Commit aborted." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
    echo "         Full report: $LOGFILE"
    exit 1
else
    echo "[RESULT] All checks passed. Proceeding with commit." | tee -a "$LOGFILE"
fi

exit 0

Here's what the legacy validation and reporting logic covers:

| # | Check | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Non-ASCII filenames** | Blocks commit if non-ASCII filenames are staged (respects `hooks.allownonascii` config) |
| 2 | **Whitespace errors** | Blocks commit on trailing whitespace, mixed indentation, etc. |
| 3 | **Shell script syntax** | Runs `sh -n` on any staged `.sh`/`.bash` files |
| 4 | **Python syntax** | Runs `python3 -m py_compile` on staged `.py` files (if Python 3 is available) |
| 5 | **Debug markers** | Warns (non-blocking) on `TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK`, `XXX`, `debugger`, `console.log` |
| 6 | **Large file guard** | Blocks commit if any staged file exceeds **5 MB** |
| 7 | **Staged file report** | Always prints a summary of staged files (`name-status`) |

A full run log is written to `/tmp/pre-commit-report.log` on every commit. The hook exits non-zero (aborting the commit) only when hard errors are found.
